Tennis Tips and Predictions for ATP, WTA and Grand Slam Tournaments

OLBG's tennis tipsters share free tennis tips and predictions for ATP Tour and WTA Tour events, including the four Grand Slams. Tips are also posted for lower-tier events such as the ATP Challenger Tour and WTA 125 tournaments, and for team competitions like the United Cup, Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

The Grand Slams and the weekly ATP and WTA Tour events usually attract the most tips, as they are widely shown on TV and streaming services. That means you can find tennis predictions for most of the big tournaments throughout the season.

Free Tennis Tips and Predictions Today

How tennis picks are listed

This page lists the most popular free tennis picks on OLBG today. Selections can cover matches and tournaments over the next week or two, so click the 'Events' column heading to sort the tennis predictions by date. Where a match is listed, the selection is for a betting market on that match. Where a tournament is listed, for example 'US Open' or 'US Open Women', the selection is for the tournament winner market. To check the upcoming schedule, see the official ATP Tour website for the men's events and the official WTA Tour website for the women's events.

Tennis betting markets we show tips for

Tournament Winner

The most popular pick under a tournament heading is the selection with the most tips to win the tournament outright. Tour events are listed by name, for example 'ATP Rome' or 'WTA Madrid'. Tournament Winner picks can also include each-way selections. Each-way terms vary by bookmaker, but they commonly pay on a player reaching the final, so check the terms before you bet. Click the most popular pick to open the tournament tips page, which shows every selection placed, including the each-way picks.

Win Match

This is a straight bet on a player to win the match, with no other conditions. The most popular pick shown for each match is the player most tipsters have selected to win. Rules on retirements and walkovers vary between bookmakers, so check your bookmaker's tennis betting rules before you place your bet.

Set Betting

These picks show the exact set score a player is tipped to win by, for example, 'Player A to win 2-0' in a best-of-three match or 'Player A to win 3-1' in a best-of-five. The odds are usually longer than for Win Match, but the exact set score must be correct for the bet to win.

Total Games

Bookmakers set a line for the total number of games in a match, for example, 20.5 games. The total is both players' games won added together. You choose 'Over' or 'Under' the line, so picks are headed 'Over' or 'Under' according to whether tipsters expect more or fewer games than the line.

1st Set Winner

This is a straight bet on who wins the first set only. It is sometimes a popular choice for tipsters backing the underdog, as a strong start against a higher-ranked player can pay off even if they go on to lose the match.

Games Won

This is a handicap market in which one player starts with a games advantage or deficit. Bookmakers set the line, for example, 'Player A -4.5', which means Player A has to win by a margin of at least 5 games across the match. If you think they will, the selection is Player A -4.5. If you think the line is too big, the alternative is to back their opponent at +4.5 games.

Tennis odds and Value Ratings

The odds for each selection are shown next to each popular pick. We always recommend looking for value tennis bets, but we know many bettors like to combine short-priced picks in accas. Click the 'Odds' column heading to sort the popular picks from shortest to longest odds, or the reverse.

The 'Value Rating' column shows a rating of up to five stars. It compares the percentage of tips a selection has received with its odds. If the share of tips is higher than the chance implied by the odds, the selection could be a value bet. Click the 'Value Rating' column heading to sort the picks by rating.

How to find more tennis tips and predictions

To see all of today's free tennis predictions for a match or tournament:

  1. Click on one of the highlighted popular picks.
  2. This opens a page showing all of the predictions for that tennis match or tournament.
  3. You will see the most popular selections for that event, along with the pick from the tipster with the best profit record on it.
  4. Scroll down to see the other markets, tipsters' analysis comments and their profit records. To compare tennis tipsters more widely, visit our best tennis tipsters page.
  5. One comment is shown for each selection, but you can click 'View all picks' to see more.
How to Bet on Our Tennis Tips

You can place a bet on our tennis tips without leaving OLBG. Use the 'Add' button next to a pick to put it on your betslip:

  1. Click 'Add' next to each tennis tip you want to back. Your selections stay on your betslip until you are ready to bet.
  2. Add as many selections as you need. Adding several lets you build accas and other multiple bets.
  3. Compare bookmakers' odds on your selections using the odds comparison at the top of the screen.
  4. Choose your bookmaker. You will be taken to their site with your selections already on the betslip, so you only need to add your stake.

New to tennis betting? Our Best Bookmaker For Tennis Betting Guide explains how to place tennis bets and compares bookmakers, with customer reviews to help you choose. If you prefer to bet on your phone, our Best Sports Betting App Guide covers the main options. Bookmakers also run free bets and betting offers for new customers, which are worth checking before you open an account.

Tennis tips are opinions, not guarantees, so only bet what you can afford to lose and check the odds when you confirm your bet, as they can change quickly. You must be 18 or over to bet. UK-licensed bookmakers offer tools such as deposit limits and time-outs to help you stay in control, and our responsible gambling guide explains how to use them. If gambling is causing you problems, free support is available from GambleAware and GamCare.
ATP Grand Slam Comparison: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open

How do the four Grand Slams differ when it comes to men's singles betting markets? The tables below compare the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open over the last 10 editions of each (roughly 1,200 completed matches per tournament), based on OLBG's analysis of Grand Slam results. Retirements and walkovers are excluded, as bookmakers often settle them differently. All Slam matches are best of five sets.

Stats last updated: after the 2026 US Open.

ATP Grand Slams: Win Match and 1st Set Winner

The favourite is the player with the shorter pre-match price. The final column shows how often the player who won the opening set went on to win the match.

Grand SlamSurfaceFavourite wins matchFavourite wins 1st set1st set winner wins match
Australian OpenHard76.5%68.5%78.1%
French OpenClay76.8%70.2%80.1%
WimbledonGrass76.8%68.4%76.4%
US OpenHard73.6%68.2%74.9%

Favourites win roughly three matches in four at every Slam, with the US Open producing the most upsets. The French Open stands out for first-set conversion: the opening-set winner goes on to win the match around 80% of the time, compared with about 75% at the US Open. Taking the first set matters most for the underdog. At the French Open, an underdog who wins the first set goes on to win the match more often than at Wimbledon (55.6% against 49.6%).

ATP Grand Slams: Set Betting

Share of completed matches finishing with each set score, from the winner's perspective.

Straight-sets wins are the most common result everywhere, with the French Open highest. About one match in five goes the full five sets, with the Australian Open slightly ahead. The US Open has the highest share of 3-1 finishes.

Wimbledon produces the most games and the most tiebreaks, while the French Open produces the fewest. The gap between the two is around two games per match on average. The lines above are illustrative, so always compare against the line your bookmaker actually offers.

ATP Grand Slams: Games Won

Average winning margin in games, and how often the favourite won by more than a given number of games (a favourite who loses never covers).

Grand SlamAverage winning marginFavourite covers -3.5Favourite covers -5.5Favourite covers -7.5

Wimbledon6.165.1%49.6%29.8%
US Open6.664.2%53.4%36.2%

Winning margins are widest at the French Open and narrowest at Wimbledon, which fits the totals above: more games mean closer matches. Favourites at the French Open cover larger handicaps more often than anywhere else.
WTA Grand Slam Comparison: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open

The same comparison for women's singles, over the last 10 editions of each Slam (roughly 1,250 completed matches per tournament), based on OLBG's analysis of Grand Slam results. Retirements and walkovers are excluded. Women's Slam matches are best of three sets, so Set Betting has only two outcomes.

Stats last updated: after the 2026 US Open.

Favourites win around 71% to 74% of women's Slam matches, a few points fewer than on the men's side, and the US Open is the most favourite-friendly. The opening set is more decisive in a best-of-three: around 83% of first-set winners go on to win the match, whichever Slam it is.

Where Our Tennis Tips Come From

The tennis tips on this page are posted by OLBG tipsters, members of our community who have gone through the tipster application process. They share their picks and reasoning for free, and tips cover everything from Grand Slam match winners to set betting and total games, so you can see how many tipsters have backed a selection before you decide.

Each popular pick shows how many tipsters have backed it, and many come with a comment explaining the reasoning. Open a tip to see every selection placed on that match or tournament, along with the tipsters' analysis. Tennis Betting Tips FAQs

  • This page lists the most popular free tennis tips from OLBG tipsters for ATP Tour, WTA Tour and Grand Slam events, plus lower-tier tournaments and team events such as the United Cup, Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup. Click any pick to see every selection placed on that match or tournament, along with tipsters' comments.

  • We show tips for Win Match, 1st Set Winner, Set Betting (the exact set score), Total Games (over or under a line), Games Won (a games handicap) and Tournament Winner for outright bets. Each market is explained in the section on the tennis betting markets we show tips for.

  • The Value Rating is a score of up to five stars. It compares the share of tips a selection has received with the chance implied by its odds. If the share of tips is higher than the odds suggest, the selection could be a value bet. It is a guide, not a guarantee, and you can click the column heading to sort picks by rating.

  • In our analysis of the last 10 editions of each Grand Slam, Wimbledon has produced the most games per match on average in both men's and women's singles. The French Open has produced the fewest in the men's event. See the ATP and WTA Grand Slam comparison tables above for the full Total Games breakdown.

  • In our analysis of the last 10 editions of each Grand Slam, the winner of the opening set has gone on to win roughly three men's matches in four, or four in five at the French Open. In women's matches, which are best of three sets, it is more than four in five. This is useful context for the 1st Set Winner and Win Match markets.

  • Rules vary between bookmakers. Many settle Win Match bets on the official result if a player retires once the match has started, but bets are often void if a player withdraws or walks over before play begins.
